subject: ent
title: Diseases of the external ear

steps.tx: The **external ear** collects sound through the pinna and external auditory canal to the tympanic membrane. The outer canal is cartilaginous with glands and hair, the inner canal is bony and exquisitely tender, which explains pain patterns in disease. Congenital atresia, prominent ears and microtia matter cosmetically and for hearing development in children.
steps.say: The pinna and canal funnel sound to the drum. The bony inner canal hurts easily. Birth canal defects affect appearance and hearing development.

steps.tx: **Otitis externa** inflames canal skin, often after water exposure or cotton bud trauma, causing itch then severe pain worsened by tragus pressure or jaw movement. Discharge, canal swelling and debris block hearing temporarily. Pseudomonas dominates in swimmers and diabetics, while Aspergillus and Candida cause itchy fungal disease with visible spores after prolonged topical antibiotics.
steps.say: Swimmer's ear hurts when the tragus is pressed. Pseudomonas follows water exposure; fungi follow long topical antibiotics. Pain out of proportion needs care.

steps.tx: Impacted **wax** is treated only when symptomatic, causing blockage, deafness or masking the drum, and removed by syringing only with an intact drum and no infection history, or by microsuction and instruments under vision. Auricular haematoma from trauma must be drained and compressed, otherwise repeated bleeding destroys cartilage into cauliflower ear.
steps.say: Treat wax only when it blocks or deafs. Never syringe a perforated drum blindly. Drain and compress ear haematomas to save cartilage shape.

steps.tx: **Malignant (necrotising) otitis externa** is a skull base osteomyelitis of the canal in elderly diabetics or immunosuppressed patients, almost always pseudomonal. Nocturnal deep pain, granulations at the bone cartilage junction and cranial nerve palsies signal spread. It demands prolonged antipseudomonal therapy and imaging, never simple ear drops alone.
steps.say: In elderly diabetics, deep night pain with canal granulations means skull base infection until disproven. That needs systemic antipseudomonal treatment and scans.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Perichondritis infects pinna cartilage after trauma, piercing or burns, sparing the lobule which has no cartilage, while relapsing polychondritis is autoimmune and recurrent. Canal furuncle is a staphylococcal hair follicle abscess of the outer canal. Herpes zoster oticus (Ramsay Hunt) blisters the concha with facial palsy when varicella zoster reactivates in the geniculate ganglion.
steps.say: Lobule sparing points to cartilage disease of the pinna. Ramsay Hunt blisters the ear and paralyses the face from shingles reactivation.
